healthcareSystem: Universal public (free for citizens, tourist hospitals separate)
qualityNotes: Cuba has a strong primary care system with high doctor-to-patient ratios. However, hospitals often lack modern equipment and medications due to economic constraints. Tourist hospitals (Clínica Internacional) offer better care but at higher cost.
pharmacyHours: State pharmacies typically open 8am-5pm Mon-Sat. Limited stock is common. Tourist pharmacies in hotels have better availability but higher prices.
pharmacyTips: Medication shortages are common throughout Cuba. BRING EVERYTHING YOU NEED from home — do not rely on finding medications locally. Even basic items like ibuprofen and bandages may be unavailable.
prescriptionRules: Cuba's pharmacy system is state-controlled. Foreign prescriptions are not recognized. A Cuban doctor can write prescriptions, but availability of medications is the real issue.

restrictedMeds.name: Most controlled substances
restrictedMeds.note: Bring documentation for any prescription medications

restrictedMeds.name: Large quantities of any medication
restrictedMeds.note: Customs may question large amounts — carry a doctor's letter explaining the need

bringDocumentation: Bring ALL medications you'll need for your entire trip plus extras. Cuba has chronic medication shortages. Carry a doctor's letter for prescription medications. Keep medications in original packaging.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Travel health insurance is MANDATORY for all visitors to Cuba. You must show proof of coverage at immigration. Policies must cover medical expenses in Cuba specifically.
travelInsurance.tips: Cuba requires proof of health insurance at entry. Some airlines include basic coverage with your ticket. If not, purchase a policy from Asistur (Cuba's state insurer) at the airport — though buying in advance is recommended. US-based insurance may not be accepted.

required: Yellow Fever (if arriving from endemic area)
vaccinations.notes: Hepatitis A and Typhoid strongly recommended due to variable food/water hygiene outside tourist resorts.

waterNotes: Do NOT drink tap water in Cuba. Always drink bottled or purified water. Ice in tourist hotels is generally safe (made from purified water), but be cautious with ice at street vendors.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants (paladares and state restaurants). Be cautious with street food and raw vegetables/salads outside tourist areas. Fruit you can peel yourself is safest.
medicalTourismNote: Cuba is known for medical tourism, particularly for eye surgery, orthopedics, and skin treatments (vitiligo). Costs are significantly lower than Western countries.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Cuba. Mandatory travel insurance, medication shortages, emergency numbers, vaccination requirements, and water safety tips.

hospitals.name: Clínica Central Cira García
hospitals.notes: Designated foreigners' clinic. International standard. Payment in CUC/USD.

hospitals.name: Hospital Hermanos Ameijeiras
hospitals.notes: Major public hospital. Some doctors speak English.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache
pharmacyPhrases.local: Necesito medicina para el dolor de cabeza

dentalCare.availability: Dental care available but supplies may be limited. Clínica Cira García serves foreigners.
dentalCare.notes: Cuba has well-trained dentists but limited supplies and equipment. Bring dental supplies if you have ongoing dental needs.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Go to Clínica Cira García for dental emergencies. Bring cash as payment.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: Contact your embassy or Clínica Cira García
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited English-speaking mental health services. Most counseling in Cuba is in Spanish; international hotels in Havana and Varadero can sometimes arrange referrals.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services in English are very limited. Contact your embassy for assistance.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Cuba's accessibility is very limited. Havana's colonial architecture includes many steps and narrow sidewalks.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Clínica Cira García has some wheelchair access. Other facilities are limited.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Classic cars used as taxis are not wheelchair friendly.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Cuba is very challenging for wheelchair users. Plan carefully and consider hiring a private driver with an accessible vehicle.

covidStatus.notes: Cuba removed COVID entry requirements. Bring sufficient medications as pharmacies may have limited stock.

insuranceClaimProcess: Travel insurance is required for Cuba entry. Clínica Cira García handles foreigner billing. Pay in cash (USD/EUR) and keep all receipts. Cuban medical documentation may need translation for insurance claims.
